faq.q: What is a line of symmetry?
faq.a: A line of symmetry splits a shape into two halves that match exactly, like a mirror image. If you fold along it, the halves fit on top of each other.
In capital letters, A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X and Y have an up-down line, and B, C, D, E, H, I, K, O and X have a side-to-side line. It can depend on the font.

faq.q: Can a shape have more than one line of symmetry?
faq.a: Yes. A rectangle has 2 lines, a square has 4, and a circle has endless lines of symmetry through its centre.
asks: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?

faq.q: Why does F have no line of symmetry?
faq.a: F has its arms pointing only to the right. No fold, up-down or side-to-side, makes one half land exactly on the other.

faq.q: How can I test for symmetry?
faq.a: Trace the shape, cut it out and fold it. Or stand a small mirror on the line: if the shape looks whole in the mirror, it is a line of symmetry.
asks: How do I check for symmetry?

facts: A square has 4 lines of symmetry and a rectangle has 2.
A circle has an endless number of lines of symmetry.
The Taj Mahal in Agra, India, is famous for its symmetry.
